short: A decisive naval battle that eliminated the Imperial Japanese Navy's ability to conduct large-scale carrier actions.
full:
Fought from 19 to 20 June 1944, the Battle of the Philippine Sea was the largest carrier-to-carrier battle in history. It occurred during the United States' amphibious invasion of the Mariana Islands. The Imperial Japanese Navy sortied its combined fleet to force a decisive battle, hoping to halt the American advance across the central Pacific.

The engagement resulted in a disastrous defeat for Japan. American radar, superior aircraft like the F6F Hellcat, and well-trained pilots decimated the Japanese attacking waves in what became known as the "Great Marianas Turkey Shoot." The Japanese lost three aircraft carriers and roughly six hundred aircraft, representing the bulk of their remaining naval air power. They never managed to replace these devastating losses in skilled pilots and aircrews.
